questions.question: What should be the least five digit number that on dividing by 3, 7, 13 and 37 give 2 as remainder?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The numbers **3, 7, 13, and 37** are all **prime numbers**.

Their **LCM** is simply their product: 3 × 7 × 13 × 37 = **10101**.

This is already the least **five-digit number** divisible by all four.

To get a **remainder of 2**, simply add 2 to this LCM: 10101 + 2 = 10103.

**∴ The correct answer is 10103.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: **3, 7, 13, 37**

Remainder: **2**

**Formula:** Required Number = **LCM(Divisors) × k + Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af59e8b136107bf863d679d201b889832a32d4ebccd1b61739c84f45b02dfc31.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM(3, 7, 13, 37) = 3 × 7 × 13 × 37

⇒ 21 × 13 × 37

⇒ 273 × 37

⇒ 10101

The number must be of the form 10101k + 2.

For the least **five-digit number**, we take k = 1:

⇒ Number = 10101 × 1 + 2

⇒ Number = 10101 + 2

⇒ Number = 10103

**∴ The correct answer is 10103.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Remainder Rule

If a number gives the same remainder **R** when divided by a, b, and c, then the general form is **LCM(a, b, c) × k + R**.

LCM of Prime Numbers

The **Least Common Multiple** of any set of prime numbers is always equal to their **product**.

Divisibility by 10101

The number **10101** is a unique number that can be expressed as **3 × 7 × 13 × 37** or 101 × 100 + 1.</p

questions.question: Prokaryotes are included under the Kingdom of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Monera__**.

__
 
• A **prokaryote** is a relatively simple **single-celled organism**.

 
 
• They come under the kingdom of **Monera.**
 
 
 
• **Eukaryotes are complex organisms (including all multi-celled organisms)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Whittaker** proposed an elaborate **five-kingdom classification – Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.**
 
• **Carl Woese** proposed a **six-kingdom classification - Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, Protista, Archaea/Archaebacteria, and Bacteria/Eubacteria.**
 
• In the six-kingdom classification, **Monera** was divided into two parts **Archaea and Eubacteria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
 

 MONERA (EUBACTERIA & ARCHAEA)
 
 
 
• **Prokaryotic**, unicellular organisms.
 
• No cell nucleus nor any other membrane-bound organelles within their cells.
 
 
 
 

 PROTISTA
 
 
 
• Green, golden, red, and brown unicellular algae large, single eukaryotic cell.

• Multicellular, with a cell wall, organelles including a nucleus, but no chloroplasts.
 
• They have no mechanisms for locomotion.

• Multicellular form with specialized eukaryotic cells.
 
• Do not have their own means of locomotion.
 
 
 
 

 ANIMALIA
 
 
 
• Multicellular form with specialized eukaryotic cells.
 
• They have their own means of locomotion.

questions.question: 30% of the men are over the age of 25 years, and 80% are under or equal to 50 years of age. Football is played by 20% of all men. What percentage of football players are under or equal to 50 years of age, if 20% of men over the age of 50 years play football?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let total number of men = 100

⇒ 80 men are less than or equal to 50 years old

(Since 80% of the men are less than or equal to 50 years old)

⇒ 20 men are above 50 years old

(Since we assumed total number of men as 100)

20% of the men above the age of 50 play football.

Number of men above the age of 50 who play football

⇒ (20 × 20)/100 = 4

Number of men who play football = 20 (Since 20% of all men play football)

Percentage of men who play football above the age of 50,

⇒ 4/20*100 =20%

Percentage of men who play football less than or equal to the age 50,

⇒ 100% − 20% = 80%

**Therefore the answer is 80%.**

questions.question: The ability of a cell to divide into two equal daughter cells is called_________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****__binary fission__**.

__
 
• The ability of a cell to divide into two equal daughter cells is called **binary fission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The organism duplicates the genetic material, or deoxyribonucleic acid ( DNA), in the binary fission process and then breaks into two parts (cytokinesis), each new organism receiving a single copy of DNA.
 
• **Multicellular fragmentation** is a type of asexual reproduction in which an organism is divided into fragments.
 
• **Multiple fission **is the asexual reproduction process, in which many daughter cells are produced from the parent cell instead of 2 daughter cells.
 
• **Budding **is a form of asexual reproduction in which, due to cell division at one particular location, a new organism emerges from an outgrowth or bud.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Fragmentation, multiple fission, binary fission, and budding are all types of asexual reproduction methods in organisms.

 
• **Fragmentation:** This is a form of asexual reproduction where a new organism grows from a fragment of the parent. Each fragment develops into a mature, fully grown individual. This occurs in many organisms such as starfish, sea anemones, and planaria, as well as in many plants, fungi and bacteria.
 
• **Multiple Fission**: In this method, an organism divides into many new individuals simultaneously. The parent organism undergoes cytokinesis (cell division) to form several daughter cells. This is common in some protists like Plasmodium (the organism that causes malaria) and certain types of algae.
 
• **Binary Fission:** In this mode of reproduction, a parent organism, usually a single cell, splits into two separate cells. Binary fission takes place in many unicellular organisms such as bacteria and protozoa.
 
• **Budding**: This is a form of asexual reproduction in which a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud on another one. The new organism remains attached to the parent organism to begin with, eventually separating and living independently. Budding is common in yeast and hydra.

questions.question: P and Q are two numbers such that if P increased by 20 percent and Q decreased by 40 percent, their sum remains constant. By what percent P is greater than Q?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

When P increased by 20% & Q decreased by 40%, their sum remained constant.

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

P + Q = 120% of P + 60% of Q

P + Q = 6/5 of P + 3/5 of Q

6P/5 - P = Q - 3Q/5 ⇒P/5 = 2Q/5

P = 2Q ⇒ P/Q = 2/1

Percentage by which P greater than Q is,

(2 - 1)/1 × 100 = 100% 

**Hence, the correct answer is 100%.**

questions.question: Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, provides for

options.text: Rights of minorities to establish educational institutions
Education for weaker sections of the country
Giving financial assistance to less advanced states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free and compulsory primary education**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Article 45 under Directive Principles of State Policy** laid down the foundation stone of **free and compulsory education in the country**. The article states that “** **the state shall endeavour to provide, within a period of ten years from the commencement of this constitution, for **free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years**”. **Article 45 recognizes the child’s right to get an education and directs the state: **
 
• To make primary education compulsory and available to all;
 
• To encourage the development of different forms of secondary education, including general and vocational education, make them accessible and available to every child,** **and take appropriate measures such as the** **introduction of free education and offering financial assistance in case of need.
 
• Equality of educational** **opportunity** **can not be denied to anyone under **Article 29(2) **according to which **admission cannot be refused to anyone on the basis of race, caste, the language** in any institution maintained by the state or aided by the state.
 
• Also, the** five articles - 15, 29(2), 15(3), 46 and 29(l) **entrust the** responsibility of equalization of educational opportunity i**n all parts of the country to the Government of India and to that end, to give special assistance to backward areas or states.
 
• It is therefore clear that the task of** **providing universal educational opportunity to all children of the country is the **joint responsibility** of the central government, state governments, and local bodies as well as voluntary organizations.
 
• The central government, in respect of primary education, has some important roles to play such as initiating researches and pilot projects in elementary education, providing financial assistance to states, acting as a coordinating agency between state and other international agencies, and sorting out the differences between various states, ensuring equitable distribution of resources and inequality of opportunities, etc. 

**Hence, we conclude that Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, provides for ​Free and compulsory primary education.**

questions.question: If a reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for ₹250, then the original price of rice per kg is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Savings due to price reduction = 10% of ₹250 = ₹25.

This saved amount allows the purchase of the extra 22 kg at the new reduced price.

New price per kg = ₹25 ÷ 22.

Original price per kg = New price ÷ 90% = (25 ÷ 22) × (100 ÷ 90) = 250 ÷ 198.

Original price ≈ ₹1.26.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1.26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹250

Reduction in price = 10%

Increase in quantity = 22 kg

**Concept Used:**

When the total expenditure remains constant, Price and Consumption (Quantity) are inversely proportional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/780edb7551a9bb2e69acd85c7dab7e93ce3adcc87c2dc297091e649b22ff2367.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price Ratio (Original : New) = 100 : 90 = 10 : 9

⇒ Consumption Ratio (Original : New) = 9 : 10

⇒ Increase in consumption ratio = 10 − 9 = 1 unit

⇒ 1 unit = 22 kg

⇒ Original Consumption = 9 units = 9 × 22 = 198 kg

⇒ Original Price = Total Amount ÷ Original Consumption

⇒ Original Price = 250 ÷ 198 = 1.2626... ≈ ₹1.26

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1.26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price and Consumption Relation

When total expenditure remains constant, price and consumption are inversely proportional (Price × Consumption = Constant). If price ratio is a : b, consumption ratio becomes b : a.

Base Change Method

If the price of a commodity decreases by x%, the consumption can be increased by (x ÷ (100 − x)) × 100% without increasing the total expenditure.

Successive Percentage Change

The net percentage change formula is a + b + (a × b ÷ 100). This applies when multiple percentage changes occur on a base value successively.

questions.question: By selling 24 items, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 4 items. His gain percentage is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the **gain** is equal to the **Selling Price (SP)** of **y** items on selling **x** items:

**Gain %** = [y ÷ (x − y)] × 100

Here, x = 24 and y = 4.

**Gain %** = [4 ÷ (24 − 4)] × 100 = (4 ÷ 20) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of items sold = 24

**Profit** = **Selling Price (SP)** of 4 items

**Formula Used:**

**Profit** = **Selling Price (SP)** − **Cost Price (CP)**

**Gain %** = (**Profit** ÷ **CP**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad9c1fb05e38a4c1a8112c5312ecbf3940f35e942c66ee36d6a437bfa321581d.png] 

⇒ Let **SP** of 1 item = ₹1

⇒ **SP** of 24 items = 24 × 1 = ₹24

⇒ **Profit** = **SP** of 4 items = 4 × 1 = ₹4

⇒ **CP** of 24 items = **SP** of 24 items − **Profit**

⇒ **CP** of 24 items = ₹24 − ₹4 = ₹20

⇒ **Gain %** = (4 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ **Gain %** = 1/5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Selling Price

If a seller loses the **SP** of **y** items by selling **x** items, the **Loss %** = [y ÷ (x + y)] × 100.

Profit and Loss on Cost Price

If the **Profit** is the **CP** of **y** items by selling **x** items, the **Gain %** = (y ÷ x) × 100.

Basic Relation

**Cost Price (CP)** = **Selling Price (SP)** × [100 ÷ (100 + **Gain %**)].

questions.question: From a container having pure milk, 35% is replaced by water and the process is repeated thrice. At the end of the third operation. the purity of the milk is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Milk **Final Concentration** = Initial Concentration × (1 − Replacement Fraction)ⁿ

Replacement fraction = 35% = 35/100 = 7/20

Remaining fraction per operation = 1 − 7/20 = 13/20

After 3 operations, Purity = 100% × (13/20)³ = 100% × (2197/8000) = 2197/80 %

2197/80 = 27 (37/80) %

**∴ The correct answer is 27(37)/(80)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1aef5690f353d2d7e6237e87a37655c5a7fb1c508138a8dec0c6e0b713e7009.png] 

**Formula:** Final Quantity = Initial Quantity × (1 − x/V)ⁿ

⇒ Let **Initial Quantity** of pure milk be 100 units.

⇒ Milk after 1st operation = 100 × (1 − 35/100) = 100 × 65/100 = 65 units.

⇒ Milk after 2nd operation = 65 × (1 − 35/100) = 65 × 13/20 = 845/20 = 42.25 units.

⇒ Milk after 3rd operation = 42.25 × (13/20) = 549.25/20 = 27.4625 units.

⇒ In fraction form: 100 × (13/20) × (13/20) × (13/20) = 100 × (2197/8000)

⇒ Final Purity = 2197/80 % = 27 (37/80) %

**∴ The correct answer is 27(37)/(80)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Repeated Replacement Formula

When a certain quantity 'x' is removed from total volume 'V' and replaced by another liquid 'n' times, the **Final Liquid Quantity** = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.

Ratio of Milk and Water

The ratio of **Milk to Water** after n operations is [V(1 − x/V)ⁿ] : [V − V(1 − x/V)ⁿ].

Successive Percentage Change

This problem is a case of **Successive Percentage Decrease**, similar to the **Depreciation** formula in Compound Interest.</p

questions.question: At what percentage above the Cost Price must an article be marked so that after giving 5% discount a shopkeeper may gain 33% of profit.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for **Mark-up Percentage**:

Mark-up % = [(Profit% + Discount%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)] × 100

Mark-up % = [(33 + 5) ÷ (100 − 5)] × 100

Mark-up % = (38 ÷ 95) × 100 = (2 ÷ 5) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit = 33%, Discount = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73d814191fc51e78a51dc9540419c5902040c2b2f8608023d88cdf82d44f3a0f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100

⇒ Since Profit = 33%, **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 33 = 133

⇒ SP is obtained after a 5% discount on **Marked Price (MP)**

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 5) / 100

⇒ 133 = MP × 95 / 100

⇒ MP = (133 × 100) ÷ 95

⇒ MP = 140

⇒ **Mark-up** = MP − CP = 140 − 100 = 40

⇒ Mark-up % = (Mark-up ÷ CP) × 100 = (40 ÷ 100) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

**__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio between **Marked Price** and **Cost Price** is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the **Effective Discount** = [a + b − (a × b)/100]%.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**, whereas Profit or Loss is generally calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**.</p

questions.question: If X is 90 % of Y, what percentage of X is Y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume Y = 100.

Since X is 90% of Y, then X = 90.

Percentage of X that is Y = (Y ÷ X) × 100

Required % = (100 ÷ 90) × 100 = 1000 ÷ 9 = 111.11...

**∴ The correct answer is 111.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

X = 90% of Y

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Value ÷ Base) × 100

 
 Y (Total Base) = 100 units
 
 X (90% of Y) = 90 units
 
• 
 To find: (Y / X) × 100 = (100 / 90) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ X = (90 ÷ 100) × Y

⇒ X = 0.9 × Y

⇒ Y = X ÷ 0.9

⇒ Y = (10 ÷ 9) × X

⇒ Percentage of X that is Y = (Y ÷ X) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = [(10/9)X ÷ X] × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (10 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 1000 ÷ 9

⇒ Required Percentage ≈ 111.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 111.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100% more than A.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert any fraction a/b to a percentage, multiply it by 100. Common conversion: 1/9 ≈ 11.11%.

Basic Percentage Formula

Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100. The "Whole" is always the value following the word "of" or "than".</p

questions.question: If the radius of the cone is increased by 10% and the height of the cone is increased by 20%, find the percentage increase in the volume of the cone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Volume of a Cone** is proportional to r²h.

Effective change in r² (two successive 10% increases) → 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

Total change in **Volume** (combining 21% for r² and 20% for h) → 21 + 20 + (21 × 20)/100.

Change = 41 + 4.2 = 45.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Increase in **Radius** (r) = 10% and increase in **Height** (h) = 20%.

**Formula Used:** Volume of Cone (V) = (1/3) × π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5cb69195f64dfba0aa9c2f00c05410b38e79d004f76ad6c79ec5f7e780e8f35.png] 

⇒ Let the initial radius be r and initial height be h.

⇒ Initial Volume (V₁) = (1/3) × π × r² × h

⇒ New Radius (r') = r + 10% of r = 1.1r

⇒ New Height (h') = h + 20% of h = 1.2h

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = (1/3) × π × (1.1r)² × (1.2h)

⇒ V₂ = (1/3) × π × 1.21r² × 1.2h

⇒ V₂ = 1.452 × [(1/3) × π × r² × h] = 1.452 × V₁

⇒ **Percentage Increase** = (V₂ − V₁)/V₁ × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = (1.452 − 1) × 100 = 0.452 × 100 = 45.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 45.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

Volume Dependency

If the volume depends on dimensions as V ∝ xmyⁿ, the ratio of new volume to old volume is (xₙₑw/xₒₗd)m × (yₙₑw/yₒₗd)ⁿ.

Cylinder and Cone Relation

A **Cylinder** and a **Cone** with the same radius and height have volumes in the ratio 3 : 1. Any percentage change in dimensions affects both identically.</p

**Argument II** is also strong because manufacturers and traders may benefit from a single GST as it will simplify their tax obligations and reduce the compliance burden. This, in turn, may lead to increased compliance and boost tax collection.

**Argument III** is weak because the fact that no other country has adopted such a system does not necessarily mean that it is not a good idea for India. The Indian economy has its own unique characteristics and challenges, and it may require a different approach to tax collection and management than other countries.

So, both argument I and argument II are strong, while argument III is weak.

Hence, The correct answer is **"Only arguments I and II are strong".**

questions.question: The famous 'Trimurti' sculpture is present in which of the following caves?

__
 
• The 'Trimurti' sculpture is located in the **Elephanta Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site near Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• The sculpture depicts the **three faces of Lord Shiva**, representing his roles as the Creator (Brahma), Preserver (Vishnu), and Destroyer (Mahesh).
 
• This colossal statue is carved in relief, measuring approximately **20 feet in height**, and is considered one of the finest examples of ancient Indian rock-cut art.
 
• The Elephanta Caves date back to the **5th–7th century CE**, and the Trimurti is the central figure of the main cave, known as the Great Cave or Cave 1.
 
• The caves are attributed to the **Shaivite faith** and reflect the rich cultural and religious heritage of India.

• Located on Elephanta Island (Gharapuri Island) in Mumbai Harbour, about 10 km from the Gateway of India.
 
• These caves are divided into two groups: **Hindu caves** (dedicated to Lord Shiva) and **Buddhist caves**.
 
• The island was named "Elephanta" by Portuguese explorers after they found a large stone elephant statue there.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Trimurti:**
 
 
• The Trimurti embodies the concept of the cosmic functions of creation, preservation, and destruction in Hinduism.
 
• The three heads symbolize **Satvik (purity), Rajasik (passion), and Tamasik (destruction)** aspects of existence.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Style:**
 
 
• The caves are an excellent example of **Gupta-era architecture**, showcasing intricate carvings and iconography.
 
• The Trimurti relief is considered a masterpiece of Indian art and is an iconic representation of rock-cut sculpture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Elephanta Caves were designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 1987 for their outstanding universal value.
 
• They are preserved as an important cultural heritage of India.

questions.question: Which organisation releases the Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report

The correct answer is __**UNESCO**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• The **Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report** is an annual publication released by the **United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).** 

• The GEM Report was first published in **2016** and serves as a continuation of the earlier **Education for All Global Monitoring Reports**. 

• The primary objective of the GEM Report is to **monitor the progress of education systems** globally and assess the implementation of **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4)**, which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education. 

• The report provides a comprehensive analysis of global education trends, policies, and challenges, covering aspects like **access, equity, quality, and financing of education**. 

• Each annual report has a **specific theme**. For instance, the 2023 GEM Report focuses on **technology and education**, addressing how digital tools can support learning and the challenges of digital divides. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **UNESCO:** 
 

• **UNESCO** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** established in **1945** with its headquarters in **Paris, France**. 

• Its mission is to promote **international collaboration in education, science, culture, and communication** to contribute to peace and security. 

• UNESCO is responsible for monitoring progress toward **SDG 4** of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which focuses on education. 

• It works in areas such as **literacy, teacher training, gender equality in education, and digital education**. 
 
 

• **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4):** 
 

• SDG 4 is one of the 17 goals under the **United Nations 2030 Agenda**. 

• Its main aim is to **“Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.”** 

• The goal focuses on aspects like **universal primary and secondary education**, eliminating gender disparities, improving literacy rates, and ensuring quality education. 
 
 

• **Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report Themes:** 
 

• Each year, the GEM Report focuses on a unique theme related to education. Examples of past themes include:

questions.question: Which of the following HTTP response codes indicates that the requested resource was not found?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

The HTTP response code **404** indicates that the requested resource could not be found on the server. This status is commonly returned when a user attempts to access a webpage or resource that does not exist or has been moved without updating the corresponding link.

**Common Causes:**

 
• Incorrect URL entered by the user.
 
• Broken or outdated links pointing to resources that have been deleted or moved.
 
• Server misconfiguration or permissions issues preventing access to the resource.

**How 404 is Represented:**

When a 404 error occurs, most servers display a user-friendly error page with a message like "Page Not Found" or "The requested URL was not found on this server." These pages often include navigation options to help users find what they are looking for.

**Best Practices for Handling 404 Errors:**

 
• **Custom Error Pages:** Design a helpful error page that guides users to navigate back to the homepage or search for other content.
 
• **Redirects:** Implement URL redirects to direct users from outdated links to the correct location.
 
• **Regular Link Maintenance:** Periodically check and update links on your website to ensure they point to valid resources.
 
• **Search Functionality:** Provide a search bar on the error page to allow users to find related content.

questions.question: According to the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, which of the following is NOT one of the five stages involved in the approach to estimating monetisation potential?

The approach to estimating the monetisation potential under NMP 2.0 follows a structured 5-stage methodology:

 
• **Identification of the Asset Classes:** Selecting specific brownfield assets across 12 sectors (Highways, Railways, etc.) that are ready for monetisation.
 
• **Determination of suitable mode of monetisation:** Choosing between models like **InvITs** (Infrastructure Investment Trusts), **REITs**, or contractual models like **OMT** (Operate-Maintain-Transfer).
 
• **Estimation of monetisation value:** Calculating the potential financial value of individual assets.
 
• **Estimation of ‘Aggregate Monetisation Value’:** Compiling the total value to reach the national target (estimated at **₹16.72 Lakh Crore**).
 
• **Allocation of proceeds from monetisation:** Strategizing how the generated funds will be recycled into new greenfield infrastructure projects.

• **Land Exclusion:** Under the NMP framework, the **direct permanent sale of public land** is generally excluded, as the primary goal is "Capital Recycling" where the government retains ultimate ownership of the core infrastructure.
 
• **Brownfield Focus:** The pipeline focuses on **de-risked, brownfield assets** that are already operational and generating revenue.

questions.question: What does the 'D' in DRAM stand for?

The correct answer is __Dynamic Random Access Memory__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• DRAM stands for Dynamic Random Access Memory.
 
• DRAM is a type of memory that is used in computers and other devices to store data dynamically.
 
 
• It requires periodic refreshing of the data to retain the information stored in it.
 
 
 
• DRAM is widely used as the main memory in computers because of its cost-effectiveness and ability to store large amounts of data.
 
• It is characterized by its need for constant power supply to maintain the stored data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• DRAM is different from SRAM (Static Random Access Memory) which does not need to be periodically refreshed and is faster but more expensive.
 
• Memory in computing refers to the processes used to acquire, store, retain, and later retrieve information.

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a solid right circular cylinder of height h and radius r is one-third of its total surface area, then:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of CSA to TSA for a right circular cylinder is CSA / TSA = h / (h + r).

Given CSA is one-third of TSA, so CSA / TSA = 1 / 3.

Equating the ratios: h / (h + r) = 1 / 3

⇒ 3h = h + r

⇒ 2h = r ⇒ h = (1/2)r

**∴ The correct answer is h = (1/2)r.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04ea252f9d04475afc2898a69f7011af0cf89a407f09da4fe97c631cf9411147.png] 

**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = (1/3) × Total Surface Area (TSA)

**Formula Used:**

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

TSA of cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = (1/3) × 2πr(h + r)

⇒ 2πrh ÷ 2πr(h + r) = 1/3

⇒ h / (h + r) = 1/3

⇒ 3 × h = 1 × (h + r)

⇒ 3h = h + r

⇒ 2h = r

⇒ h = (1/2)r

**∴ The correct answer is h = (1/2)r.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder is given by the formula V = πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Surface Area of Cone

The curved surface area of a cone is πrl and the total surface area is πr(l + r), where l is the slant height.

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is 4πr², as it does not have flat surfaces, its CSA and TSA are the same.
